activities.sample: I kept reaching the far end of the store and realizing that one item was back near the entrance. Before the next trip, I copied the list into the order of the aisles and put uncertain items in a separate section. After two trips I moved frozen food to the end because the checkout line was sometimes long.

activities.context: Helping arrange seats for a community gathering.
activities.sample: The first seating plan fit everyone on paper, but it put the people arriving late behind chairs they would have to move. I marked which seats needed a clear path, shifted two tables, and kept four flexible seats near the door until everyone arrived.

The lowest monthly payment looked best until I wrote down the total paid at one year, three years, and the full term. I added a row for what I would still owe if I stopped early, because that changed which option was actually cheaper for me.

known_self_description: I like helping people and explain things clearly.

activities.context: Explaining an online form to relatives.
activities.sample: I first wrote a full page of instructions, but two people stopped at the same screen. I replaced that paragraph with one screenshot and a circle around the button. Then I asked someone who had never used the form to try it without me talking.

activities.context: Using AI to draft an announcement.
activities.sample: The draft sounded polished but several people could read the deadline two different ways. I asked for three interpretations of the sentence, chose the shortest wording that removed the ambiguity, and tested it by asking two people what date they thought it meant.

activities.context: Leaving instructions for a substitute volunteer.
activities.sample: Instead of listing everything in the order I usually do it, I separated what must happen before opening from what can wait. I added a short section called 'If only one thing goes wrong' because that was the situation where a new person would be least sure what mattered.
